reviews.title: Useful but...
reviews.text:
4 vs. 5 because it has not yet been fully "cleaned up" - i.e. non-AA stuff has not yet been removed.

This app was originally developed by a Chinese developer in China whose identity for a very long time was extremely difficult to uncover. Kudos to Alcoholics Anonymous for doing the hard work of finally tracking the developer down, acquiring the app, and taking it over. As a result, right now at the end of September 2026, the app is still being modified and edited so that it indeed conforms to AA's legacies and can be used and relied upon as "approved" literature. 

For example, if the version you download here still has a "Joe and Charlie..." feature, know that those will likely be edited out eventually or incorporated elsewhere as simply examples of the application of the program practiced by these 2 alcoholics - neither of whom were "special" or experts in the application of AA's principles to living sober.  

The entire program of alcoholics anonymous is focused on humility, which is why AA is very careful not to 'deaconize' any individual member; in fact, that is the whole basis of the program of alcoholics anonymous and why, even after 70 years or so, "anonymity" remains the mechanism which sustains it - nobody is in charge and nobody is better qualified and skilled in living sober in AA than anybody else. Contrary to popular opinion, the primary purpose of anonymity in AA is not to keep secrets - it is to keep the egotism of "AA experts" in check.

All sober members of AA have is their personal and collective experience but that is in fact their "secret" to success.

reviews.title: Thanks, Ben.
reviews.text: I just wanted to say thank you to the original developer of the app. Since the sale of this app to the official Alcoholics Anonymous World Services, he’s no longer in charge of things, so I don’t know if he’ll see this but I have to try. Free access to AA literature is a life saving resource, for those willing to use it, and I owe my life to the principles taught to me by the program of AA. Thank you developers, past and future. Please continue to make access to the most effective treatment for the disease of addiction available to as many people as possible, just like the 12th step says—We try to carry the life saving message of AA to all that suffer from alcoholism and to practice the spiritual principles we learn through the program in every area of our lives. Keep up the good work.

reviews.title: This will save my life
reviews.text:
I am four days sober. I have been in denial about my addiction to alcohol my whole life. Until I earned myself a DUI a few days ago. 
My alcoholism has hurt my family, compromised my marriage, and caused me to live and act with bad judgement- which could have hurt or killed someone. 
This app and this program give me the hope that I can turn my life around and be the person that I used to strive to be. 
If not for this awakening and this support, I may well have run my full life into ruin or worse. 
I am grateful that I am alive and that this program and this app are here to help me.

I recommend this app for anyone who is looking for AA info, readings, meetings, prayers etc this app is all you need!

reviews.title: A great help
reviews.text: In the mornings, I could easily freak out with fear and worry. Self-pity and anxiety can take over, especially after coffee I can grow uncomfortable in my own skin.  I have the disease of alcoholism, which is not my fault.  However, at 59 years old, I need to keep being grateful for my life and reasonably good health. I can’t see the future which kept me drinking and getting high, which for a long time helped me enjoy being in the moment. But without any real plan or design for living. It’s been almost a year since my mother passed away and through God‘s grace I’ve been able to stay in our family home and obtain employment that I’ve been able. To keep doing the next right thing.
